Want to Write Your First Novel? Here Are 10 Books to Read Before Picking Up Your Pen.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1702 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Entrepreneur

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, you have an idea for a fiction novel that you can’t stop thinking about.
  • According to recent reports, so you open a blank document, type a sentence, pause for a moment, then delete it.
  • Sources indicate that before you try to answer every question on your own, turn to your bookshelf.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you have an idea for a fiction novel that you can’t stop thinking about. Maybe it’s a character, a setting or a scene you’ve played out in your head countless times. No matter what it is, you want to explore this fresh world.

According to recent reports, so you open a blank document, type a sentence, pause for a moment, then delete it. Faced with an empty page, you wonder how your seed of an idea is supposed to become an entire book. How can a formless thought take shape?

Sources indicate that before you try to answer every question on your own, turn to your bookshelf. Learn the craft of writing from people who have done it before you. How does a writer make you care about a stranger, a made-up character, within the first few lines? What keeps you reading when little seems to happen?

Then there’s the ending. How does an ending feel both surprising and inevitable?

The following 10 books offer a place to explore those questions. Some explain how to build a plot or develop a character. Others help you manage doubt and pay attention. They all treat fiction as a craft you can study. They can also keep you company as you begin writing a story of your own and remind you that you are not alone in your pursuit of writing a novel.

On Writing: A Memoir of the Craft.

Author Stephen King has published over 60 novels and sold more than 350 million copies of his books globally. In this book, he combines his personal story of becoming a writer with a practical account of how he works. In the autobiographical sections, he reveals his early encounters with storytelling, his struggles before getting published for the first time and how writing fits into the rest of his life. He also explores the practical aspects of writing, including vocabulary, grammar, description, dialogue and revision. His approach is direct and conversational. The book also features a marked-up manuscript that indicates actual revisions, which can be helpful for writers thinking about the process of editing. Overall, King offers encouragement and technical advice for first-time novelists.

Bird by Bird: Some Instructions on Writing and Life.

According to recent reports, anne Lamott starts this book with a family story. Her brother left a report about birds until the last minute and felt overwhelmed by everything he had to do. Their father told him to take it bird by bird, inspiring the title of the book. That small instruction becomes the book’s central approach to writing. Instead of confronting the project as an impossible whole, attend to one manageable piece at a time. Lamott applies that approach to rough drafts and the emotional confusion of creative work. She offers humor and permission to produce messy drafts. Her advice is to reduce the task into bite-sized parts, accept imperfection and continue even when there is no guarantee of a future reward.

Writing Down the Bones: Freeing the Writer Within.

In this book, popular author Natalie Goldberg approaches writing as a practice strengthened through repetition. She offers short reflections and exercises that help writers get words onto the page before their inner judgment shuts them down. The exercises provide a low-pressure space for discovering memories, images and even unexpected connections. The focus is on developing an open relationship with the act of writing. Goldberg pushes writers to keep the hand moving and resist the urge to cross out thoughts immediately. These small habits help the writer notice more and censor less when creating material. If you spend more time evaluating possible sentences rather than writing them, this is the book for you. It has sold more than one million copies.

Story Genius: How to Use Brain Science to Go Beyond Outlining and Write a Riveting Novel (Before You Waste Three Years Writing 327 Pages That Go Nowhere).

Author Lisa Cron is a story coach, speaker and author who has previously worked as a literary agent. She asks writers to look beneath the surface events of a story. In other words, an unusual situation or dramatic accident is not enough by itself. What matters is how that event affects a particular person, given that person’s unique worldview. Her method places the protagonist’s internal struggle at the center of the novel’s development. The book moves from an initial idea to a developed blueprint, including scenes. Its aim is to connect incidents through a protagonist’s changing interiority. Read this when you know what happens in your novel but cannot explain why it matters to the main character living through it.

Save the Cat! Writes a Novel: The Last Book On Novel Writing You’ll Ever Need.

Sources indicate that jessica Brody is the bestselling author of more than 20 novels, mainly young adult fiction. This book organizes story structure around 15 major developments, extending from the opening image to the finale. It also introduces 10 story categories based on patterns of conflict and transformation, giving writers ways to understand the kind of narrative they are building. The appeal is clarity. The writer can examine the purpose of different turning points in their novel. What debuts the central journey? When does the situation change? How does the ending express what the protagonist has learned? Read this if your first novel feels exciting in fragments but isn’t coming together as a whole.

Plot & Structure (Write Great Fiction).

Former trial lawyer James Scott Bell offers a practical guide to creating a plot and understanding how its parts fit together. He addresses the relationship between plot and structure and the differences between commercial and literary fiction. The emphasis is on usable techniques. Bell’s central framework is called LOCK, which stands for lead, objective, confrontation and knockout. These elements direct attention toward a compelling central character, a clear goal, meaningful opposition and a strong ending. Using these attributes, you can decide if a story has enough pressure and direction to sustain the reader’s interest. What is your protagonist trying to achieve? What prevents success? What would make the resolution satisfying?

Steering the Craft: A Twenty-First-Century Guide to Sailing the Sea of Story.

Author Ursula K. Le Guin turns her attention to the language by which a story reaches the reader. Her writing guide combines discussion with exercises. She walks readers through drills in storytelling, point of view and grammar. The exercises make this a book to use actively. Le Guin says that the work of a sentence is to carry the reader to the next one. She addresses how to handle exposition, or how to incorporate information into a story instead of allowing explanation to bring it to a halt. Her approach connects elements sometimes treated separately, like language and pacing. The value of this book is helping readers hear and inspect their prose. A promising plot still needs solid sentences that keep the story moving.

This style manual was privately printed in 1918 for Cornell University students by English professor William Strunk Jr., then published more widely by Harcourt in 1920. Strunk’s former student and author E. B. White revised and expanded the volume in 1959. This book concentrates on constructing clear prose. It is short, about 100 pages, which means it is perfect to consult regularly as you write. Its usefulness lies in directing a writer’s attention toward language. A novelist might be absorbed in a character’s choices while giving too little thought to how to clearly communicate those behaviors in a sentence. Strunk and White set the stage for authors to learn the conventions of clear prose. They provide a foundation from which to make deliberate stylistic choices that enhance a reader’s experience.

The Writing Life: The Classic Essay Collection on the Creative Process.

Annie Dillard, a Pulitzer Prize-winning novelist with experience writing fiction and nonfiction, published poetry, essays, prose and literary criticism. In The Writing Life, she offers a reflection on creative writing, not a step-by-step manual. She considers the difficulty and uncertainty of the writing process. A line of words can lead a writer into unfamiliar territory, but they may not know where to go next. What first appears promising might actually be a dead end, while a seemingly incidental encounter might become the real subject. Dillard preserves a place for the parts of writing that remain difficult, even when the writer is attentive and experienced. She offers perspective on the patience and seriousness of writing.

Refuse to Be Done: How to Write and Rewrite a Novel in Three Drafts.

Sources indicate that writer and teacher Matt Bell treats revision as a central part of novel writing. His guide divides the process into three broad stages, giving each step a different purpose. The first move helps writers generate material and move through the initial draft. The second focuses on reworking the narrative through outlining, modeling and rewriting. The third step turns toward a layered polishing process. This final stage breaks revision into specific operations, deconstructing a large and potentially overwhelming task into a series of more manageable actions. This book is worth reading before writing the first page. It offers a practical guide to making a manuscript stronger.

Ahmed Barakat is a journalist and copywriter based in Georgia with a growing focus on blockchain technology, DeFi, AI, privacy, digital assets, and fintech innovation.

Industry observers note that the CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Sources indicate that A Monero token crashed 99% on Friday after 5.2 million XMR1 tokens moved from a wallet tied to its creator, triggering a massive sell-off on Hyperliquid. The token, issued through crypto swap service Wagyu, plunged from around $494 to below $1 in 35 minutes. The wallet receiving the tokens sold enough to generate $13.22 million in USDC before converting the proceeds into 7,467 ETH.

Industry observers note that wagyu’s wallet security and the backing behind its wrapped Monero product are being questioned. And the sell-off also sent shockwaves through the Monero market, although native XMR remained a separate asset from the collapsing XMR1 market.

Industry observers note that the incident began this morning when the account responsible for deploying XMR1 transferred tokens to a newly created wallet. Blockchain intelligence firm Bitquery identified three separate transfers between 04:46 and 05:16 UTC. Two transactions moved 100,000 XMR1 each, followed by a much larger transfer of 5 million tokens.

Industry observers note that the receiving wallet had been created that morning. It began selling shortly after receiving the tokens, overwhelming buyers on Hyperliquid’s order book. XMR1 had traded near $500 throughout the previous week. Its price then collapsed to about $1 within roughly 35 minutes, leaving holders with almost nothing.

Sources indicate that bitquery traced 363,804 tokens sold for $13.5 million. The remaining 4.83 million tokens stayed in the receiving wallet during its investigation. The sell-off also exposed how concentrated XMR1’s supply had been. Before the transfers, its deployer account still controlled 93% of the token’s supply.

Hyperliquid transfers require signatures from the account’s own key, rather than an ordinary trading API wallet. This means whoever authorized the transfers likely had access to the deployer’s main key. Whether someone stole that access or used it legitimately remains unknown.

Discover: The Best Token Presales.

The damage extended beyond traders watching XMR1 collapse on their screens. Bitquery matched the seller’s transactions against 388 accounts that purchased the dumped tokens. One buyer alone paid $3.56 million, while 27 large buyers accounted for 77% of the total proceeds.

The wallet did not leave the money sitting in USDC. It began moving funds through Hyperliquid’s bridge into Arbitrum shortly after selling.

XMR1 hack: 388 Hyperliquid buyers paid $13.50 million for a token that fell 99.8%https://t.co/k5ggHcH6Al.

On Arbitrum, the wallet exchanged $13.22 million in USDC for 7,467 ETH through CoW Protocol. It then routed much of the Ethereum through Socket, Mayan, and Stargate. 6,810 ETH then arrived on Ethereum after those bridge transactions. Approximately 4,836 ETH landed in a newly created wallet that had not sent any funds onward.

Sources indicate that the investigation also identified 7,348 ETH across three wallets during its tracking window. That left a substantial amount of the proceeds sitting outside the original trading account.

Recent findings suggest that the incident has put Wagyu’s bridge infrastructure under scrutiny. XMR1 represents Monero on Hyperliquid and is issued through Wagyu’s bridging service. Users can move native XMR into the service and receive XMR1 for trading. They can also reverse the process to recover their Monero.

Native XMR did not suffer the same collapse. Monero continued trading around $470–$482, while XMR1 lost virtually all its market value.

Holders now face a difficult question: Can they still exchange their remaining XMR1 for native Monero?

Industry observers note that the incident also comes weeks after Wagyu disclosed a separate data leak on October 28. Researchers identified exposed records potentially linking crypto deposits, Monero receiving addresses, and customer IP addresses.

Wagyu previously said customer funds remained unaffected by that incident. No established connection links the October leak to Friday’s wallet transfers.

Sources indicate that the latest investigation also uncovered another potential concern. The same deployer account controls 99.97% of ZEC1, a separate token representing Zcash on Hyperliquid.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Decentralized artificial intelligence (AI) network Gonka AI has reportedly suffered a massive security attack in which hackers exploited its Ethereum bridge to withdraw stablecoins and glitch unbacked tokens worth over $1 million.
  • According to blockchain analytics firm Onchain Lens, the hacker was able to gain access to the bridge's BLS group key, allowing the attacker to withdraw funds and problem Wrapped Gonka (WGNK) tokens without backing them with the required assets.
  • Per the report, the hacker managed to withdraw $884,800 in Tether (USDT) and USD Coin (USDC) stablecoins and also issued $172,000 in unbacked WGNK tokens.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Decentralized artificial intelligence (AI) network Gonka AI has reportedly suffered a massive security attack in which hackers exploited its Ethereum bridge to withdraw stablecoins and glitch unbacked tokens worth over $1 million.

According to blockchain analytics firm Onchain Lens, the hacker was able to gain access to the bridge's BLS group key, allowing the attacker to withdraw funds and problem Wrapped Gonka (WGNK) tokens without backing them with the required assets.

Per the report, the hacker managed to withdraw $884,800 in Tether (USDT) and USD Coin (USDC) stablecoins and also issued $172,000 in unbacked WGNK tokens.

Combined, the total value of the affected assets stood at around $1.06 million, per Onchain Lens.

Following the hack, the funds were transferred through the decentralized exchange Uniswap and multiple crypto wallets, making it challenging to trace their final destination.

In a recent development, the attack targeted Gonka AI's cross-chain bridge. The cross-chain bridge makes it possible to transfer assets from Gonka AI's native chain to Ethereum and vice versa.

According to the project's technical documentation, withdrawing funds from Gonka to Ethereum requires certain cryptographic signatures from the network's validator set.

The cryptographic signatures are checked against the BLS group key, which changes with every network epoch.

Per the report, the attacker was able to change the epoch BLS group key on the bridge, making it possible for the hacker to control the part of the bridge responsible for authorizing fund withdrawals.

Thus, the hacker was able to withdraw funds from the bridge's stablecoin reserves and concern WGNK tokens without locking the required amount of assets on the native blockchain.

Blockchain security firm Blockaid noted that the hack had taken place, with the total amount of funds stolen reaching about $1.05 million across roughly five transactions at the time of the initial alert.

At the time it spotted the suspicious activity, Blockaid noted that the hack was still ongoing.

Onchain Lens's numbers differ slightly, with the firm reporting around $884,800 in stablecoin withdrawals and $172,000 in unbacked WGNK issuance.

Notably, the issuance of unbacked tokens presents an additional problem, given that such tokens could potentially enter circulation without the necessary reserves to back them.

High-end genealogy travel is booming, offering luxe journeys to the roots of your family tree

💡 Key Takeaways
  • My great-great-grandfather came to the Tuscan ghost island of Pianosa as a prisoner.
  • The island lives up to its name, I thought as my ferry drifted toward the sole dock on this protected isola fantasma.
  • In a recent development, I’d learned this family lore thanks to a partnership between Ancestry, the Blackstone-owned leader in the at-home DNA-testing space, and Kensington, a bespoke travel outfitter, which invited me to test-drive its Personal Heritage Journey.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My great-great-grandfather came to the Tuscan ghost island of Pianosa as a prisoner. I arrived there on a luxury vacation.

The island lives up to its name, I thought as my ferry drifted toward the sole dock on this protected isola fantasma. “Pianosa” is derived from piano, Italian for “flat,” and indeed the island crouches low to the cyan Tyrrhenian Sea, its shores fringed by parasol pines and deserted prison watchtowers. From 1856 to 1998, Pianosa was a remote penal colony—and the place where my ancestor, Salvatore Giovanni Pellegrino Irace, died.

In a recent development, I’d learned this family lore thanks to a partnership between Ancestry, the Blackstone-owned leader in the at-home DNA-testing space, and Kensington, a bespoke travel outfitter, which invited me to test-drive its Personal Heritage Journey. After I submitted a DNA sample, Ancestry got to work filling in my Italian family tree, with researchers combing archives in Tuscany, Molise, and Campania. “So the interesting thing about Salvatore,” genealogist Kyle Betit mentioned on our initial call, “is that he died in prison of tuberculosis in 1894—and we don’t know why he was there.”.

In a recent development, who doesn’t love a good family mystery? That’s part of what draws clients to Kensington’s genealogical-based trips. The journeys average $20,000 to $25,000 per person, with the company’s travel desk handling all the details in high style.

For me, that meant a chartered boat from mainland Tuscany to the island of Elba; chauffeured SUVs between regions; a private guide in Pompeii; and some spectacular accommodations, including Casa Angelina and Palazzo Avino on the Amalfi Coast. The major flex, though, was having a professional genealogist, Gabriele Musumeci, riding shotgun.

In a recent development, once upon a time, possessing one’s comprehensive genealogy was a signal of wealth and pedigree. Then, in the 2000s, the rise of at-home DNA-testing kits from Ancestry and 23andMe made such knowledge commonplace. The ultrawealthy can now seek out deeper stories through first-person ancestry tourism, from China to Ghana. Kensington reports that demand has doubled and revenue has quadrupled in five years. Grand View Research put the global value of “heritage tourism”—of which ancestral travel is a segment—at $625 billion in 2025. It’s expected to reach almost a trillion by 2033.

Recent findings suggest that “I think there’s a deep need in any of us to understand who we are,” Musumeci said as we descended the concrete steps to Pianosa’s white-sand beach, Cala Giovanna. “For most Americans, your story is cut.” He made a chopping motion. And then a sewing motion: “We stitch it back together.”.

Most luxury travel planners now offer some variety of ancestry service. Alexandrea Padilha, director at the membership-based Fischer Unlimited, recently hired genealogists in Germany and the U.S. to trace a Louisiana tech entrepreneur’s ancestry. The results were bound into a book for the client’s father’s 80th birthday and also informed the itinerary for a trip to Germany—a way to show younger family members their roots. “I think that’s grounding for young adults today,” Padilha says, “living in a world that’s slowly slipping away.”.

Sources indicate that existential dread is one hell of a motivator. “When it feels like the world may be shifting every second, people reach for something enduring,” says Dr. Katie Blake, a Texas-based social psychologist who specializes in travel. “The archives give you the facts, but it’s the place itself that gives you the identity pull that’s different than something you just see on paper.”.

According to recent reports, A sudden, biblical rainstorm broke open during our mile-long bike ride from Cala Giovanna to Pianosa’s imposing Agrippa Prison. We sheltered inside the Zante wing, where prisoners like Salvatore slept four to a concrete cell on metal beds, as thunder rattled the rusty gates.

My itinerary traced Salvatore’s life backward. A few days later, Musumeci and I rendezvoused in Molise, where Salvatore grew up. My great-great-great-grandfather, Vincenzo, moved his family to Montenero di Bisaccia, a mountain keep surrounded by vineyards and wheat fields sloping down to the Adriatic, in 1838, when Salvatore was a boy. At Montenero’s city hall, the clerks hauled out massive, crimson-bound books, and Musumeci leafed through until he found the birth and marriage records of Salvatore’s second son, Giuseppe—my great-grandfather.

Recent findings suggest that walking through Montenero’s hilltop puzzle of alleys brought those pieces of paper to life—and conjured a story of downward mobility. Along the town’s outer promenade, ringing the remains of medieval stone walls, a lookout faced the amber foothills where Vincenzo bought land and a farmhouse. I walked the narrow alley the family lived on after they lost the farm. Within four years, Vincenzo had spiraled from merchant and farm owner to street sweeper. He died in 1842, leaving his son on the poverty-to-prison pipeline.

I also saw the house in the old ghetto where my great-grandmother, Nicoletta, grew up. She and Giuseppe had a daughter out of wedlock, Mattia. (Nobody in my family had known Mattia existed until Musumeci discovered her.) The infant likely died during the couple’s 1900 journey to America, where, at Ellis Island, Irace became Erace. Giuseppe and Nicoletta settled in Philadelphia and had 16—yes, 16—more children, including my paternal grandfather, Michael Erace, who died in 2013.

In a recent development, it was like I was looking at Grandpop Mike’s long-lost brother when we met Bruno Irace, a 74-year-old Ironman triathlete and my fourth cousin, that afternoon. Smile, hair, complexion, bone structure; it was uncanny. We sipped espresso and compared photos, then visited a cemetery where “Irace” seemed to be engraved on every other gravestone. Two Iraces were listed on an obelisk in the village park honoring fallen soldiers. When it was time to leave Montenero, Bruno told us to come back soon. “You have family here,” he noted.

Sources indicate that the name Irace was also everywhere in the archives of San Luca, the family’s neighborhood church, in Praiano, on the Amalfi Coast, the final stop on my journey. This dramatic shoreline of improbable cliff-top villages and citrus groves set high above the sapphire sea is one of the most beautiful places in the world. I couldn’t help but wonder about the Iraces: Why did these fools leave? What misfortune befell my reasonably prosperous ancestors to make them abscond from this stunning seaside real estate?

Musumeci had coordinated with the pastor, who granted us free rein of his office, a charmingly cluttered room with sea views through diamond-paned windows. Hundreds of books, some dating to the 1600s, filled a tall cabinet, their yellowed pages brittle as autumn leaves. Handwritten in meticulous script were the births and baptisms, marriages and deaths of San Luca’s parishioners, which included generations of Iraces.

According to recent reports, “Oh, wow … ” Musumeci stopped suddenly as his finger moved across a page. He pointed to Vincenzo’s marriage record. “Adam, the date … ” October 10, 1807.

In a recent development, it took a few seconds to dawn on me. I checked my phone: October 10, 2026. Exactly 219 years earlier, Vincenzo Irace and Mariangela Rispoli, ages 21 and 18, had stood at San Luca’s resplendent altar and exchanged vows. Until then, I’d encountered Vincenzo mostly through his losses: his farm, his livelihood, his family’s good name. Here was a record of a beginning. Whatever came later, my great-great-great-grandparents had first been two young people at the altar of a church above the sea.

It has been revealed that I hadn’t found all the answers in Italy. We never learned why they left the Amalfi Coast, what sent their son to prison, or what compelled their grandson to cross an ocean. The private guides, chauffeured SUVs, and beautiful hotels couldn’t make the records yield answers they didn’t contain.

But the distance between my ancestors’ lives and my own no longer seemed quite so great. Standing in San Luca, I wasn’t the discerning traveler whose preferences shaped the itinerary. For all the choices I’d made on this trip, the ones that mattered most had been made two centuries earlier.

For once, the point wasn’t being made to feel important. The real privilege was the opportunity to feel very, very small.

This article appears in the December 2026/January 2027 glitch of Fortune with the headline “The most exclusive itinerary is written in your DNA.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, widely known as CZ, has expressed his concerns about the storage of sensitive personal data after Japanese authorities called on rental car services to delete customers' identity documents following a massive data breach.

In a recent development, in his latest X post, CZ pointed to a Nov. 18 notice issued by Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC). The notice urges rental car services to be cautious about unnecessarily storing images of driver’s licenses and other government-issued identification documents.

The recent call by Japanese authorities comes after a massive cybersecurity attack on a popular Japanese car-sharing service called Times Car, operated by Park24 Group.

The incident began when the manufacturer noticed suspicious activity on its system on Sept. 25. As a result, it rolled out an investigation into whether someone had accessed its systems without permission, potentially exposing customer data.

Recent findings suggest that as per the disclosure by Park24 on Oct. 23, about 6.63 million customer accounts were impacted by the breach.

Worse, the investigation uncovered evidence that hackers had transmitted 1,464,800 encrypted images of identification documents, including driver’s licenses, to external locations.

Besides that, another 891,602 encrypted images of identification documents were accessed suspiciously. However, investigators found no evidence that these additional ID images had been transmitted outside the firm’s systems.

Japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission issued its notice on Nov. 18, focusing on the risks of retaining sensitive personal data even after its original purpose has been fulfilled.

The regulatory body stressed that storing unnecessary identification images could significantly worsen the consequences of cyberattacks.

Although Japan’s latest warning specifically targets the rental car industry, CZ’s decision to share his concerns about this glitch also raises questions about personal data protection in the crypto industry.

Generally, centralized crypto exchanges require users to go through a Know Your Customer (KYC) process to access their trading platforms.

Depending on the platform and jurisdiction, these processes may require consumers to provide photos of their passports, driver’s licenses, national ID cards, and other sensitive information.

This kind of sensitive data can be a goldmine for cybercriminals, who can exploit stolen personal information for various activities such as identity theft, phishing attacks, fraudulent registrations, and more.

  • Just as the Industrial Revolution transformed business through machines, mass production and long-distance transportation, AI may be powering a new entrepreneurial boom.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

Just as the Industrial Revolution transformed business through machines, mass production and long-distance transportation, AI may be powering a new entrepreneurial boom.

We’ve seen this before: New technology dramatically lowers the cost of starting and running a business. But where the steam engine and electricity offered only a first step, still requiring substantial capital for machinery, factories and workers, AI offers modern entrepreneurs a full staircase. Today, an aspiring founder with a good idea can access powerful capabilities with little more than a computer and a Wi-Fi connection. The challenge is knowing what you need to launch and grow a business at each stage.

In a recent development, business creation has surged in 2026, with nearly every month setting a record for new registrations compared with the same month in previous years. Since January, 5.9 million new businesses have been formed nationwide — up 16% from the same period in 2025 and 24% from 2024.

What’s driving that growth? It’s not a single engine but a combination of forces, including the continued popularity of remote work and the appeal of being your own boss and having more financial freedom, both now more within reach because of AI.

If you previously dropped a business idea because it seemed too complicated or expensive, now may be the time to reconsider. AI has reached a level of capability that didn’t exist just a few years ago. It’s steadily eroding traditional startup barriers, helping founders turn even ambitious ideas into real businesses with less money, fewer employees and fewer outside resources.

Industry observers note that until recently, launching a firm often meant spending money before making money. Office space, equipment, expensive software and employees with specialized skills were requirements in most sectors, not to mention the accountants and consultants needed just to get started.

Industry observers note that now, cloud infrastructure has replaced costly servers. No-code platforms make it possible to build websites and apps without extensive programming knowledge. E-commerce platforms give small companies access to national and global markets. Generative AI accelerates this trend by helping entrepreneurs research markets, analyze competitors, draft business prepares, develop marketing campaigns, create content and automate tedious administrative work.

It has been revealed that start by asking yourself, “What do I need to reach customers at this stage, and how will it maximize my return on investment?” Use inexpensive tools to create a product prototype, a landing page or a basic marketing campaign. Talk to potential customers. Test your pricing and measure the response. Save major investments for ideas that show real demand.

AI gives founders a chance to rethink hiring. Entrepreneurs once had to hire employees or contractors before they were generating enough revenue to support them. Today, a solo founder with the right AI tools can handle many of those functions alone.

That doesn’t mean putting complete trust in a chatbot. AI-assisted work still requires human oversight, judgment, verification and refinement. And when you’re building a trustworthy brand from scratch, you have to consider accuracy, privacy and legal problems.

According to recent reports, use AI to draft routine marketing emails, but hire an experienced marketer when strategy matters. Organize basic finances with bookkeeping software, but consult an accountant for important tax decisions. Automate answers to repetitive customer service questions, but keep a human in the loop for complicated interactions or when customers ask for one. The goal isn’t to eliminate employees. It’s to delay fixed expenses until your business can support them.

Industry observers note that historically, founders moved to places like San Francisco or Austin because those cities offered concentrated pools of money and talent. Those hubs remain vibrant, but AI and remote technology are reducing the importance of location.

A tech founder in a small town can use the same AI platforms and cloud services as someone in Silicon Valley. Remote collaboration provides access to talent anywhere, and e-commerce can reach customers far beyond a company’s hometown.

Industry observers note that with AI tools, you can explore many ideas from almost anywhere. Instead of asking, “Where does my business need to be based?” you can ask, “Where would I like to live while I grow my business?” That kind of freedom can make a real difference in your quality of life.

Sources indicate that forming a business and building a successful one are different things. Many of the companies registered this year will never become fully operational. Others will struggle to find customers or stay profitable. AI can’t fix a weak business model, create demand where none exists or eliminate the financial risks of entrepreneurship.

Industry observers note that what AI can do is make the process easier and cheaper, and therein lies the lesson. Instead of investing heavily up front in one untested concept, make a series of small bets. Develop a minimum viable product. Test marketing messages. Experiment with prices. Ask AI to identify the assumptions in your business initiative, then test them with real customers and real-world data.

In a recent development, with more than 5 million businesses formed since the start of 2026, the U.S. could finish the year with close to 7 million latest registrations if the current pace continues. There’s evidence that AI may be contributing to that momentum. But like the steam engine, electricity, the internet and smartphones before it, AI is a tool. The real power lies with entrepreneurs who are willing to start lean, test early, automate selectively and spend strategically. With that approach, we may see a boom not only in startups with potential but, more importantly, in businesses that endure.

‘Sister isn’t free’: Melinda French Gates fact-checks viral ‘SNL’ sketch on eldercare

  • The sketch, a fake commercial, stars host John Mulaney as a man who has found an easy way to care for his aging father without upending his own life: “Sister,” an “elder care system” that is free and is, in fact, his sister.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 18, 2026 at 1:23 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 1:23 pm.

A “Saturday Night Live” skit about caring for aging relatives touched a viral nerve after it aired over the weekend, including with Melinda French Gates, who offered her own “fact check” on the too-close-to-home comedy.

The sketch, a fake commercial, stars host John Mulaney as a man who has found an easy way to care for his aging father without upending his own life: “Sister,” an “elder care system” that is free and is, in fact, his sister.

French Gates wrote on Instagram this week that the sketch “is funny because it’s a little too true.” Using research from Pivotal, her investment and philanthropic organization, she went through the ad’s claims one by one and found that most held up:.

Sister will provide. True, French Gates said, citing AARP and the National Alliance for Caregiving. Among adults ages 55 to 64, women are nearly 40% more likely than men to care for an older relative, and nearly 40% more likely to provide constant care.

According to recent reports, she’ll quit her job. “Mostly true,” at least the job part. Catalyst found that 42% of women who voluntarily left jobs in 2025 cited caregiving as the main reason.

Paid help is pricey. “True, unfortunately.” Newly introduced America puts the average home health aide at more than $6,600 a month, and 24-hour care can top $25,000.

Sources indicate that sister may break down. Also true. In the Caregiving in the U.S. 2025 report, nearly two-thirds of caregivers remarked they were under moderate or high emotional stress, and women felt the strain more than men did.

“Free” is misleading. French Gates noted Sister isn’t free; she’s the one paying for the care, in lost wages, stalled careers, thinner retirement savings and less time for her own life.

French Gates has made women’s health and caregiving central to her work since she stepped down as co-chair of the Gates Foundation in 2024.

According to recent reports, she left with $12.5 billion to put toward her work on behalf of women and families. Much of that work runs through Pivotal, the Seattle-area organization she founded to handle her philanthropy and investments. In June she pledged another $215 million for women’s health, which brought her giving in that area to more than $600 million over two years. The pledge included $10 million to the Menopause Society for better menopause care in the U.S.

The sketch has been shared widely across the country this week, in part because it lines up so closely with the research.

In its own analysis, The New York Times cited studies showing that daughters generally provide at least twice as much care to aging parents as sons do. The U.S., unlike many wealthy countries, offers no federal paid leave or long-term care insurance for family caregivers.

French Gates said she welcomed the conversation.

“I’m so glad we’re talking about this, and laughing about it,” she wrote on Instagram. “We need more honesty about what caring for loved ones really takes and why so much of that work falls to women. But I’d love for the day to come when these jokes don’t pack quite the same punch — because we’ve made it so much easier to care for the people we love.”.

Ronald Reagan stated you can achieve anything—if you don’t care who gets the credit. Abdul El-Sayed channels that wisdom with ‘TrumpCare for all’

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Democratic legislative agenda is taking shape, and healthcare is at the top as rising medical expenses were a major driver of midterm election messaging about affordability.
  • But while Democrats will hold commanding majorities in the House and Senate when the new Congress convenes in January, President Donald Trump has reminded them that he is ready to veto legislation he doesn’t like.
  • Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed—a former Detroit health official who campaigned on Medicare for all—sees a way around that by appealing to Trump’s ego.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Democratic legislative agenda is taking shape, and healthcare is at the top as rising medical expenses were a major driver of midterm election messaging about affordability.

But while Democrats will hold commanding majorities in the House and Senate when the new Congress convenes in January, President Donald Trump has reminded them that he is ready to veto legislation he doesn’t like.

Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed—a former Detroit health official who campaigned on Medicare for all—sees a way around that by appealing to Trump’s ego. On Nov. 12, he posted to social media a picture of a notional, gold-colored “TrumpCare” card, saying “Donald, this is on the table. Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave.”.

The next day, El-Sayed doubled down, assuring CNN in an interview that he wasn’t joking and insisting that he doesn’t care what the public insurance program called.

Industry observers note that “What you call it is secondary,” he added. “What it does in your life, that’s the whole point. None of us ran to name things, except for Donald Trump. Most of us ran to actually solve problems in people’s lives.”.

That got Trump’s attention. And on Saturday, he reposted on his Truth Social account El-Sayed’s initial Nov. 12 appeal. El-Sayed posted “Let’s get to work, then.”.

The gambit echoes a famous line from President Ronald Reagan in February 1988, when he spoke at a meeting of the White House Conference for a Drug Free America:.

“On my desk in the Oval Office, I have a little sign that indicates: There is no limit to what a man can do or where he can go if he doesn’t mind who gets the credit.”.

While similar statements have been attributed to others going back more than 100 years, Reagan’s line is notable as it came during the modern era of American politics, which has grown even more intensely partisan since then.

In fact, during the midterm election campaign, Trump ramped up the partisan rancor to such a level that he called El-Sayed a “jihadist” who was “on the side of the terrorists.”.

It has been revealed that but the incoming Democratic senator is ready to set that aside for the sake of expanding health coverage. On Sunday, El-Sayed noted Trump “signaled openness to the opportunity,” telling NBC’s Meet the Press with Kristen Welker that while growing up playing lacrosse, he was taught to play the ball, not the man.

“If the president is serious about leaving a lasting legacy, there is nothing better than the ultimate Trump card, a card that they can have in their back pocket from the moment they are born to the moment that they pass away that guarantees them the health care that has been so elusive in this country without premiums, co-pays, and deductibles,” he remarked.

El-Sayed also predicted that if Trump says he wants TrumpCare for all and is open to signing legislation, then a lot of Republicans in Congress will vote for it.

When asked later if he has any plans to meet with Trump or Vice President JD Vance, El-Sayed replied “those plans are in the works.”.

Minnesota Senator-Elect Peggy Flanagan, another Democrat who rode the blue tsunami, voiced similar willingness to capitalize on Trump’s desire to name things after himself.

“Call it whatever you want. I think people are ready for Medicare for all. If we have to call it TrumpCare in order to get it across the finish line, that’s fine by me,” she told CNN on Sunday.

The discussion over health coverage comes as open enrollment season is in full swing across the country, with workers getting sticker shock on how much premiums are going up for next year.

But Americans who get health insurance through their employers aren’t the only ones feeling the pain. The cost of coverage via Affordable Care Act aims is surging too after Congress didn’t renew the enhanced subsidies that were enacted during the pandemic.

If Trump makes a deal with Democrats to expand health coverage, it would be a 180 after he tried unsuccessfully to kill the Affordable Care Act during his first term.

Officially naming a upcoming health program as TrumpCare would also mark a departure from Barack Obama’s presidency, when Republican critics of the ACA blasted it as ObamaCare.

For his part, Obama embraced that moniker but quipped in 2024 that people are calling it the Affordable Care Act again.

“I noticed by the way that since it’s become popular they don’t call it ObamaCare no more,” he stated at the Democratic National Convention.

Yield-Bearing eZAR Blurs the Line Between Stablecoin and Investment Product

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1367 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • eZAR opened its rand-pegged token to the public on November 2 with R303 million in circulation.
  • Recent findings suggest that most stablecoin launches promise a token that never moves.
  • It has been revealed that according to launch reports, eZAR is now open to the public and to latest institutional partners after almost a year of pilot operations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

eZAR opened its rand-pegged token to the public on November 2 with R303 million in circulation. Its reserve yield is the feature that puts the stablecoin label to the test.

Recent findings suggest that most stablecoin launches promise a token that never moves. eZAR's disclosures say its holders can make money or lose it. The rand-pegged token went live to the public on November 2, and its fine print reads more like an investment product than a payments coin.

It has been revealed that according to launch reports, eZAR is now open to the public and to latest institutional partners after almost a year of pilot operations. The manufacturer notes R303 million worth of tokens had been issued and were in circulation as of October 30.

In a recent development, the project is a partnership between eZAR Ltd, asset manager Ninety One and AVBOB Financial Services, with AVBOB acting as lead institution and liquidity partner. CEO Sean Emery noted the team put "getting it right" ahead of "getting it significant" during the pilot. The message now is that eZAR is ready to scale.

It has been revealed that the model also departs from the typical single-issuer coin. Neobanks, retailers, insurers and payment firms can plug the token into their own branded wallets and share in the economics. Transfers between participating wallets settle within seconds at any hour and, according to the company, cost nothing.

The reserves backing eZAR are invested through a money market strategy run by Ninety One, mainly in the Ninety One Money Market Fund. Returns are distributed daily to partners after partnership fees, and each partner then decides on what terms its own customers receive a share.

It has been revealed that ninety One's head of digital assets, Adam Duxbury, described it as newly introduced rails under an old discipline. His firm has run money market strategies for 25 years, he remarked, and South Africa should build its own digital rand rather than import a dollar coin.

The framing is clever, since it presents the yield as a feature of "digital cash that can grow." Yet that same feature makes the classification question hard to avoid.

It has been revealed that the risk language is the most revealing part of the launch. eZAR describes itself as a crypto asset issued by the eZAR En Commandite Partnership. It states that the token is not legal tender, not a bank deposit and not a banking product, and that it carries no guarantee.

The details that follow set it further apart. The R1 redemption value depends on available liquidity. Money market returns can be positive or negative, so capital is at risk. Holders also own no units in the underlying fund and have no direct claim on it.

Industry observers note that "Capital at risk" rarely appears in stablecoin terms. A payments token is meant to hold its value and let customers redeem at par, yet eZAR's own documents hedge on both counts. Back in March, a market survey from Blockhouse had already noted that eZAR doesn't qualify as a stablecoin under most regulations. The live launch now tests that observation against a real product.

In the major rulebooks, the yield is the sticking point. The US GENIUS Act bars permitted payment stablecoin issuers from paying holders any form of interest or yield solely for holding, using or retaining the token. The EU's MiCA framework takes a similar line on interest. The logic is that a payment token paying a return starts to function like an unregulated deposit.

Industry observers note that the OCC issued its final GENIUS Act rules on October 21, and they confirmed that ban for covered issuers. The contested ground lies elsewhere, in who sits between the issuer and the holder. Earlier OCC proposals set a rebuttable presumption against yield arrangements run through affiliates and related third parties, whereas the statute itself names only issuers.

eZAR's design lands squarely in that gray zone. Returns flow to partners, and the partners decide how customers share in them. Whether that amounts to an issuer paying yield or a partner passing on profit is precisely the kind of question US regulators are now wrestling with, and it would be a difficult one to argue before the OCC.

eZAR doesn't operate under the US or EU regimes, so none of those rules apply to it directly. eZAR Ltd is described as an authorised financial services provider responsible for the main technology and services behind the partnership. That technology also draws on the South African Reserve Bank's Project Khokha 2, where eZAR's parent tech giant, Block Markets Africa, was a technical contributor.

This background signals a serious, institution-backed build rather than a speculative launch. Even so, the rand stablecoin field is getting crowded. ZARU debuted earlier this year as an institutional-grade rand coin, and a pattern is emerging of different models competing for the same local payments niche.

The bigger question is whether South Africa will define stablecoins narrowly, as the US and EU do, or leave room for hybrid products like this one. Because the network is permissioned, the reported circulation figure also rests on company disclosure rather than a public ledger, which makes the regulatory and disclosure framework matter even more.

Industry observers note that for everyday consumers, the appeal is easy to see. A rand token that moves in seconds, costs nothing to send and might earn a daily return makes an attractive pitch. For partners, shared infrastructure with a revenue share offers a way into digital payments without building a coin from scratch.

Industry observers note that the trade-off sits in the disclaimers. A holder who treats eZAR like a bank balance could be caught off guard by liquidity-dependent redemption, or by a money market return that dips below zero. That gap between how the product feels and how it is legally defined is where regulators tend to step in.

Recent findings suggest that eZAR is best understood as a hybrid: a payments token with an investment return attached. It may well succeed on those terms. Still, as more jurisdictions tighten the stablecoin definition around no-yield, par-redemption tokens, products like this will increasingly be judged on what they are rather than what they are called. How South African regulators treat eZAR in the coming months will show which way that debate is heading.

Can AI Hack Smart Contracts? How AI Agents Are Changing Blockchain Security

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: U

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, smart contract vulnerability scanners typically work by looking for certain patterns.
  • Industry observers note that for example, in December 2025, Anthropic released results from SCONE-bench, a smart contract benchmark of 405 contracts that were exploited in the 2020 - 2025 period.
  • To make sure the agent was not simply memorising exploits that were already published, newer vulnerabilities that had been published after their training cutoff were tested on Claude Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, and GPT-5, which were able to generate $4.6 million (simulated stolen funds).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, smart contract vulnerability scanners typically work by looking for certain patterns. However, because an AI agent can iterate and make use of dependencies, local blockchain forks, and decompilation, it weakens the protection gained by keeping source code secret, and can attempt attacks against complex vulnerabilities such as access control bugs, accounting errors, oracle-related bugs and unexpected contract interactions.

Industry observers note that for example, in December 2025, Anthropic released results from SCONE-bench, a smart contract benchmark of 405 contracts that were exploited in the 2020 - 2025 period. They were able to reproduce exploits for 207 contracts, totalling $550.1 million (simulated stolen funds).

To make sure the agent was not simply memorising exploits that were already published, newer vulnerabilities that had been published after their training cutoff were tested on Claude Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, and GPT-5, which were able to generate $4.6 million (simulated stolen funds).

Finally, they analysed 2,849 recent smart contracts with no known issues, discovering two previously unknown vulnerabilities that could have resulted in $3,694 (simulated stolen funds), emphasising the ability of AI agents to discover latest vulnerabilities rather than simply exploiting known ones.

Anthropic emphasised that no actual funds were lost during these experiments. It should also be noted that in one of their experiments using GPT-5, it cost $3,476 for API usage, which leaves a slim (simulated) profit.

With automated hacking becoming more effective, how can we be sure that DeFi will be able to stay ahead of these AI agents? Hacken, a blockchain security firm, reported that $1.18 billion was lost in 107 crypto hacks during the third quarter of 2026. 48% of this was from exploiting smart contracts.

Of course, this doesn’t specify the cause of these hacks. Regardless, it emphasises the importance of being able to stay ahead of AIs which could be used for exploitation.

Sources indicate that chainalysis estimates that approximately $36.7 million was stolen in 2026 from DeFi protocols that had not undergone smart contract verification. It also notes AI-assisted reverse engineering as an emerging risk without attributing any particular thefts to AI.

According to recent reports, in an experiment by a16z on 20 past DeFi price manipulation exploits, apparent success rates of 50% were reduced to 10% when the researchers restricted access to transactional data that revealed the original exploit. When the researchers gave the AI some high-level information about the DeFi domain, success rates jumped to 70%.

In a recent development, in February 2026, OpenAI and Paradigm released a benchmark for evaluating agents’ abilities in the domains of vulnerability detection, patching, and exploitation using an EVM environment (EVMbench). Results revealed that GPT-5.3-Codex achieved a 71% success rate in exploitation (limited to a sandboxed environment) and 33.3% for GPT-5.

In October 2026, CyberChainBench was released, analyzing 541 exploit events across 9 Ethereum-compatible blockchains. The best-performing configuration achieved 37.5%, 43.7%, and 23.4% success rates for detection, exploitation, and patching respectively.

In a simulation, the best-performing agent profited $57.4 million from exploits on 200 exploit events that occurred after the cutoff. Some of the reported high-severity issues were evaluated and determined to not be exploitable by OpenZeppelin. Since much of the data is trained on in the public, results may be exaggerated.

Agents will continue to improve, and while current results are not an indication that AI-driven agents are responsible for large scale on-chain thefts, it is an indication that AI can find and exploit weaknesses in smart contracts given a certain environment. Given the ease with which agents can try attacking many different protocols, smaller protocols may see an uptick in exploit attempts.

It has been revealed that teams that implement rigorous testing and monitoring could have an edge over other teams. For example, AI could be used to test a contract prior to deployment, generate regression tests, and identify weird behavior on-chain. A human would still need to verify any potential concerns and sign off on changes.

Teams should continue to perform third-party audits and implement other security best practices such as limiting access to sensitive information, setting up alerts and response intends, restricting the amount of money in a wallet, making sure AI systems do not have permissions to transact without human oversight where necessary, and so on.

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

Most entrepreneurs are using AI to get work done faster. But what if it’s moving their businesses in the wrong direction?

AI can now help entrepreneurs produce marketing campaigns, research competitors, develop strategies and complete work that once took entire teams. It’s an extraordinary shift in what’s possible for a small business. But there’s a hidden risk in all that productivity. In the video above, I explore why the entrepreneurs who gain the greatest advantage from AI aren’t the ones doing more work, but the ones discovering opportunities everyone else overlooks.

That’s what I call the “Progress Illusion.” When AI makes completing tasks effortless, it’s tempting to mistake activity for achievement. But there’s a difference between the work AI completes, how customers respond, the business results that follow and the longer-term consequences. These are the four dominoes that determine whether all that activity is actually moving your business forward.

Industry observers note that finished is a status. Progress is a consequence.

In a recent development, consider a surprising study of eBay’s paid search advertising. When the company stopped running ads for searches containing its own name, researchers found that 99.5% of the lost paid-ad traffic was replaced by free search traffic. Now imagine using AI to scale that campaign because the dashboard looked impressive. You wouldn’t necessarily be scaling growth. You could be scaling waste.

The opportunity for entrepreneurs is to use AI for something far more powerful than execution: strategic foresight.

In the video, I walk through AHEAD, my five-step framework for challenging assumptions, exploring new possibilities and uncovering business opportunities you might otherwise overlook. But even smart analysis has its limits. AI can generate so many competing strategies that deciding what to do becomes a job in itself. That’s the “Analysis Trap.”.

According to recent reports, the solution is knowing when to stop researching and start acting. I call it the “Decision Line”: three questions that help you determine whether you need stronger evidence or whether it’s time to make your next move.

Because your most valuable opportunity might not be the one you’re already pursuing. It could be an entirely different direction you haven’t considered. And you don’t need a Fortune 500 strategy department to start thinking more strategically about your business.

In a recent development, AI can help you execute almost any strategy. The real competitive advantage is discovering which plan deserves to be executed.

And in the video above, I’ll show you how to start thinking differently, uncover opportunities others overlook and make your next business move with greater confidence.

The free AI Success Kit, available to download for a limited time, comes with a free chapter from my newly introduced book, The Wolf is at The Door – How to Survive and Thrive in an AI-Driven World.

Google acquires Seattle startup Howie and its AI scheduling assistant

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 18, 2026 at 2:03 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 2:03 pm.
  • Google is bringing Seattle-based Howie, maker of an AI scheduling assistant that works from your inbox, into its Google Labs division.
  • Terms of the deal were not disclosed this week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 18, 2026 at 2:03 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 2:03 pm.

Google is bringing Seattle-based Howie, maker of an AI scheduling assistant that works from your inbox, into its Google Labs division.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed this week. Google Labs, the firm’s experimental arm, announced the acquisition in a post on X, saying it “can’t wait to learn from them as we build the next generation of intuitive AI tools together for small businesses.”.

Howie CEO and co-founder Austin Petersmith stated on LinkedIn that the team will continue building Howie at Google. “Howie has always been built on top of Gmail and Google Calendar, so Google Labs is the perfect place for us to take this product to the next level,” he wrote.

According to recent reports, petersmith co-founded Howie around 2023 with CTO Dave Newman. The two first worked together in 2013 at Assembly, which Newman co-founded, and prototyped an AI assistant in 2015 before deciding the market wasn’t ready.

We’re excited to welcome Howie to Google Labs! The @Howie_ai team has spent years figuring out scheduling and calendar management. We can’t wait to learn from them as we build the next generation of intuitive AI tools together for small businesses 🤝 https://t.co/8bzjebeGdD.

Industry observers note that customers cc Howie on an email thread, and it coordinates meeting times, adds events to calendars, follows up as needed and flags scheduling conflicts. Customers set their own rules in an open-ended preferences document, such as “if it’s a pitch call, set it to 25 minutes and use Zoom.”.

Behind the scenes, Howie ran tasks through fine-tuned language models and looped in human scheduling experts when the AI wasn’t confident.

Industry observers note that howie raised a $6 million seed round led by True Ventures in September 2025, when it introduced publicly out of private beta. At the time, it had more than 1,000 paying customers, including startup founders, venture capitalists, recruiters, consultants and journalists, and was scheduling more than 5,000 meetings a week.

Sources indicate that the deal comes as Google and rivals including OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta race to build AI agents that complete tasks on behalf of consumers. Google Labs acquired music generation platform ProducerAI earlier this year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, good morning. Intuit is unwinding its biggest acquisition while betting AI can help it win customers without owning the marketing platform it once viewed as central to that effort.

It has been revealed that the QuickBooks and TurboTax parent declared Thursday it prepares to sell Mailchimp, an email marketing automation platform, to Bending Spoons for approximately $3.68 billion. The deal is expected to close in early 2027, subject to approval, with proceeds earmarked for fiscal 2027 share repurchases. Intuit paid approximately $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021. Mailchimp’s quarterly revenue fell 1% to $313 million.

In a recent development, sasan Goodarzi, CEO of Intuit (No. 231 on the Fortune 500) noted on the earnings call that Intuit still wants to help businesses manage lead-to-cash needs, but believes it can do so more effectively by building AI-powered capabilities into QuickBooks rather than owning Mailchimp.

Mailchimp sale marks strategic shift.

Sources indicate that the divestiture adds another dimension to what CFO Sandeep Aujla has called Intuit’s “reset to reaccelerate” strategy introduced in August: accepting some near-term pressure on revenue per customer to rebuild customer acquisition. The strategy includes lower upfront revenue per TurboTax customer as Intuit seeks faster customer growth.

In a recent development, the latest results offered evidence of operating momentum. For the fiscal first quarter ended Oct. 31, revenue rose 12% to $4.35 billion, while adjusted earnings per share increased 56% to $2.91. Both exceeded analyst expectations.

In my conversation with Aujla, he pointed to mid-market revenue growth of 41% and customer growth of 30% as evidence that Intuit’s major growth initiatives are gaining traction. He also emphasized management’s commitment to delivering on its promises.

But the outlook exposed pressure at Credit Karma from tighter financing conditions and changing consumer behavior.

Industry observers note that intuit now forecasts fiscal 2027 revenue of $23.08 billion to $23.37 billion, lowering its outlook to reflect slower expected growth at Credit Karma amid tighter lending conditions and changing consumer behavior. It maintained its adjusted earnings forecast of $22.88 to $23.12 a share. Neither forecast includes the pending Mailchimp sale. The stock was down about 13% in after-hours trading.

Sources indicate that aujla noted conditions have shifted since Intuit set its guidance in August, when the debate centered on whether the Federal Reserve would hold interest rates steady or lower them. He described the environment now as one of tightening, with higher rates slowing consumer demand in the categories Credit Karma serves. Lending partners are still expanding, he said, but at a slower pace.

AI reshapes Credit Karma’s customer acquisition.

At the same time, changes in how consumers seek financial information are affecting Credit Karma.

“The evolution of consumer behavior is impacting us faster than what we had anticipated,” Aujla told me.

Historically, only about 1% of Credit Karma’s customers came through search engines, he said. Now, consumers increasingly turn to AI for initial answers before visiting Credit Karma, creating a new customer acquisition challenge.

“More customers are going to AI to get the first answer,” he said.

Intuit aims to apply lessons from QuickBooks and TurboTax to improve Credit Karma’s visibility in AI-generated responses, Aujla said. AI is thus both a product opportunity and a customer acquisition challenge.

Regarding the market’s reaction, Aujla stated that during major technological shifts, whether cloud computing, mobile or now AI, “it’s just human nature to overreact to the uncertainty and the pendulum swings.” He sees the reaction as an overcorrection, with investors questioning whether companies can successfully navigate the changes.

“What we are underwriting is, in our 40-plus years of history, we’ve been able to evolve and continue to come out of every change in the marketplace,” he remarked.

In a recent development, have a good weekend. Sheryl EstradaSheryl.Estrada@fortune.com.

It has been revealed that erik Uitenbogaart was named vice president of finance and CFO at Citgo Petroleum Corporation, (No. 24) effective Nov. 16. Uitenbogaart joins Citgo from LyondellBasell, where he held roles of increasing responsibility since 2013, most recently as vice president of finance, strategy and M&A for Sustainable Solutions. He previously led LyondellBasell’s global financial planning and analysis organization. Before that, he served as controller for Europe, the Middle East and Africa at Univar Solutions and spent more than 15 years at PricewaterhouseCoopers.

Richard McPhail, EVP and CFO of The Home Depot (No. 25), was promoted to CEO, effective Nov. 23. McPhail will succeed Ted Decker, who has returned from a temporary medical leave of absence, but will step down as president and CEO, and he will continue to serve as chair of the board of directors. McPhail joined the company in 2005 and was named EVP and CFO in September 2019.

According to recent reports, jordan Broggi was promoted to EVP and CFO at The Home Depot. Broggi is a 13-year veteran of the manufacturer, most recently serving as EVP of interconnected retail. In this role, he led the online business and customer experience for the company's digital properties, as well as loyalty, credit services and payments. Broggi has held several leadership positions during his tenure, including senior vice president of finance.

Zach Davis was promoted to president and CFO at Cheniere Energy, Inc. (No. 223). Davis was previously executive vice president and CFO. Davis has served as CFO of Cheniere since August 2020 and also serves as a director and CFO of the general partner of Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P. He joined Cheniere in 2013 and previously served as SVP of finance and VP of finance and planning. Davis has over 20 years of experience, primarily in energy and infrastructure finance.

(NYSE: CDRE), a manufacturer and distributor of safety equipment, effective at the end of the year, to pursue another opportunity as CFO. Chad Appleby, who has been Cadre’s VP and treasurer since 2014, will serve as interim CFO. Cadre has initiated a search process to identify a permanent CFO.

According to recent reports, patrick Edwards was appointed SVP and CFO of Rack Room Shoes, a footwear retailer. Edwards will succeed Ernie Shore, who will retire following 33 years of service to the company. Edwards brings more than three decades of financial and accounting experience. Most recently, he held senior leadership positions with Shoe Station Group, formerly Shoe Carnival, including SVP, CFO, treasurer and secretary.

Industry observers note that karen Brown Garza was appointed CFO of Chelsea Lighting, a lighting technology and project management specialist. Most recently, she served as interim CFO and operating advisor to Arctic Industries. Repetto brings more than 35 years of experience working with global banks, community banks, and credit unions.

Anthropic had a record-breaking IPO debut on Thursday, with shares closing up 17.07% at $97.17 after raising $81.3 billion—making it the largest initial public offering in history by capital raised. The Claude maker’s big jump on its opening day of trading dispelled, for now, fears that investors’ faith in the profitability of AI was fading.

According to recent reports, however, in a upcoming article, Fortune’s Shawn Tully points to an issue he states the bulls are ignoring. “Anthropic left an enormous share of the IPO’s proceeds on the table,” Tully writes. “We’re talking about roughly $20 billion that could have flowed into spending on AI infrastructure that instead went to significant institutions, and privileged retail investors, that reaped a gigantic, one-day windfall, as well as the underwriters that will feast on big commissions they’ll receive from the clients they awarded shares at what looks like bargain prices.”.

XRP Flashes Biggest Volatility Warning Among Major Cryptocurrencies

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (433 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • XRP stands out as the cryptocurrency with the most alarming volatility warning among major digital assets, according to recent Coinbase data.
  • XRP's seven-day options-implied price move stands at 1.94 times its historical median.
  • XRP exhibits the highest premium above its own historical volatility.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

XRP stands out as the cryptocurrency with the most alarming volatility warning among major digital assets, according to recent Coinbase data. The options market indicates that traders are now preparing for price swings that could be nearly double XRP's historical seven-day price move.

XRP's seven-day options-implied price move stands at 1.94 times its historical median. This figure far exceeds similar metrics for major cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH) and Solana (SOL).

XRP exhibits the highest premium above its own historical volatility. Solana highlights the lowest premium among these four cryptocurrencies, Coinbase remarked.

It has been revealed that as the chart below indicates, the options-implied seven-day price move for XRP is around 9.6%, according to Glassnode and Coinbase data as of Nov. 17. This compares to its historical median absolute price move of about 4.9%.

Basically, this means that the options market is signaling a price swing nearly twice as large as XRP's typical seven-day price movement.

Interestingly, Solana's implied price move is also close to 9.5%, almost the same as XRP's. Yet its historical median weekly price move is much higher at about 6.5%.

The key here is that although both cryptocurrencies exhibit similarly large potential price moves, the magnitude of the expected volatility surprise is significantly greater for XRP relative to its usual trading range.

Sources indicate that for comparison, Bitcoin indicates an options-implied seven-day move of about 6%, versus its historical median of about 3.5%. For Ethereum, these numbers are about 8% and 5.1%, respectively.

Obviously, this latest figure doesn't necessarily imply that XRP is going to crash. It's a sign that options traders expect a substantial price move regardless of its direction.

Recent findings suggest that implied volatility is a forward-looking measure. It's based on options prices. The higher the implied volatility, the more traders pay for exposure to potential price movements or protection against them.

The chart from Coinbase is based on a one-standard-deviation estimate. It's derived by converting annualized at-the-money implied volatility into a seven-day timeframe.

It has been revealed that for XRP, the roughly 9.6% implied move represents a statistical range. It's not a guaranteed price target. A one-standard-deviation range suggests about a 68% chance of the price staying within this range under typical modeling assumptions.

Thus, the latest figure of 1.94x implies that XRP's volatility premium remains high despite a slight decrease from the previous reading.

Industry observers note that from XRP traders' perspective, this can be a very challenging market environment. For traders using leverage, there could be a high risk of liquidation due to potentially sharp price moves.
